**Problem**
`Daemon::apply_update` applies `BeadPatch` field-by-field inline. The patch semantics live in `src/daemon/ops.rs`, but the actual application logic lives in `src/daemon/executor.rs`, so adding or changing fields requires touching both places and is easy to miss.

**Design**
Add a helper on `BeadPatch` (e.g., `apply_to_fields(&self, fields: &mut BeadFields, stamp: &Stamp) -> Result<(), OpError>`) in `src/daemon/ops.rs`. Move the current field-application logic (including label parsing and status→workflow transition) into this helper. Update `Daemon::apply_update` to call the helper inside `apply_wal_mutation`.

**Design Notes**
Keep behavior identical: ignore `Patch::Clear` for required fields (title/description) and for labels (no-op), preserve current status validation and error messages.

**Acceptance**
- [ ] `Daemon::apply_update` delegates patch application to `BeadPatch::apply_to_fields`.
- [ ] Label validation and workflow transitions behave exactly as before.
- [ ] Tests pass.

**Files:** `src/daemon/ops.rs`, `src/daemon/executor.rs`

description:
**Problem**

`crates/beads-core/src/wire_bead.rs` carries an unconditional legacy key alias:
`resolve_field_stamp()` looks up `_v.<field>` and, for `status`, silently falls
back to `_v.workflow`. That key is the pre-rename name of the status field
(`workflow` -> `status`, see `bac6e2c9:src/core/wire_bead.rs:287`).

This is a workaround, not a design:

- The alias is consulted on **every** field-stamp read, forever, including
  steady-state v2 stores that can never contain `_v.workflow`.
- It is keyed off a bare string match in `legacy_stamp_key()`, so nothing ties
  it to the store format version that actually needs it.
- It hides the real invariant: a v2 store has exactly one spelling per field
  stamp. Today a v2 store containing `_v.workflow` would be silently accepted
  rather than rejected as corrupt.
- Any future field rename will be tempted to add another arm to the same match,
  growing an open-ended compat table in the hot read path.

**Why it exists**

Stores written before the rename put the status stamp under `_v.workflow`.
Reading them with a `"status"`-only lookup silently fell back to the bead-level
stamp, which (a) failed `closed_at`/`closed_by` validation in
`crates/beads-git/src/wire.rs` so the whole store refused to load, and (b) would
have corrupted LWW ordering for status on merge. This blocked `bd migrate to 2`
on any real pre-rename store.

**Design**

Confine the alias to the v1 read path so v2 reads never consult it.

1. Thread the store format version into bead decoding, so v1 decode and v2
   decode are distinct paths rather than one lenient path.
2. Move the `workflow` -> `status` alias into the v1 decoder only. Model it as
   part of the v1 wire schema (that format's key genuinely *is* `workflow`),
   not as a fallback bolted onto the current schema.
3. Make v2 decode strict: an unknown or legacy `_v` key is an error, not a
   silent miss that degrades to the bead-level stamp.
4. Delete `legacy_stamp_key()` and `LEGACY_STATUS_STAMP_KEY` from the shared
   `resolve_field_stamp()` path.

**Acceptance**

- [ ] `resolve_field_stamp()` has no legacy key aliasing
- [ ] v1 decode still reads `_v.workflow` as the status stamp
- [ ] v2 decode rejects a bead carrying `_v.workflow` instead of ignoring it
- [ ] `parse_state_reads_status_stamp_from_legacy_workflow_key` still passes (moved to the v1 decode surface)
- [ ] Unknown `_v` keys in a v2 store are rejected, with a test
- [ ] `cargo xtest` green

**Files:** `crates/beads-core/src/wire_bead.rs`, `crates/beads-git/src/wire.rs`

**Context:** introduced while unblocking `bd migrate to 2` on the beads-rs store
itself (952 beads, 47 of them carrying `_v.workflow`). Store migrated and pushed
as `a557114f`.
title: Remove the _v.workflow legacy stamp alias workaround
